subject: SIG Artifact Request: Change-control snapshots, CI guardrails & ephemeral creds for FedFin audit
messages:
From: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@fedfinaudit.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SIG / FedFin: Request for SDLC artifacts (change-control + CI guardrails)

Hi Hannah,

We're starting the SIG questionnaire review for FedFin's upcoming assessment window. To complete the SDLC controls section we need the following artifacts by 2028-10-24:

- A snapshot of your Change Control log covering the last 12 months (CSV preferred) showing change IDs, approvers, timestamps, and rollback flags.
- The latest SDLC runbook (developer & release runbooks) that documents gating criteria for production deploys.
- CI/CD policy excerpt that shows automated checks (PR gating, secret-scan, binary provenance), with evidence of enforcement (pipeline run IDs or timestamps).
- Description of ephemeral credential usage and short-lived token rotation for CI agents.

If any items above are sensitive, please indicate redaction and provide a short explanation of what's redacted and where we can get a verifier-friendly artifact instead.

Thanks,
Amanda Lopez
Senior Auditor — FedFin Compliance
FedFin Audit Services

---
Attachments requested: none (link references ok)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG / FedFin: Request for SDLC artifacts (change-control + CI guardrails)

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. We're able to produce the artifacts requested. Quick notes up front:

- Change-control export: we will provide a CSV export filtered for FedFin-relevant projects. It includes ticket id, author, approver, approval timestamps, and a rollback indicator. Sensitive customer PII fields are omitted.
- Runbook: we'll share the internal SDLC runbook PDF (v3) with the sections you highlighted redacted for internal-only troubleshooting logs.
- CI/CD policy snapshot: we'll attach the pipeline policy text and a pipeline run sample demonstrating PR gating + secret-scan enforcement.
- Ephemeral creds: short memo explaining our GitHub Actions/runner ephemeral token rotation and vault usage.

Neha — can you assemble the CSV, the pipeline snapshot and the run IDs from Oct 2028 so we can include specific enforcement evidence? Rishi — please confirm whether the run IDs require signed attestations or if a pipeline log excerpt is sufficient.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Trust & Risk — Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Oct 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG / FedFin: Request for SDLC artifacts (change-control + CI guardrails)

Hannah / Rishi — assembling now. Deliverables planned:

1) change-approvals-audit-trail.csv — export from change-management system (columns: change_id,ticket_key,author,approver,requested_at,approved_at,deploy_at,rollback_flag). Redacted columns: branch_compare_uri and internal_notes.
2) ci_pipeline_policy_snapshot_20281020.txt — policy rules (PR gate rules, required checks, secret-scan thresholds) plus policy IDs.
3) pipeline-run-samples.txt — 3 run IDs (pipeline: infra-deploy, run IDs: rdw-20281005-1182, rdw-20281012-1219, rdw-20281018-1307) with short descriptions showing secret-scan passed and PR gating enforced.
4) ephemeral-creds-memo.txt — brief description: CI runners authenticate to Vault using OIDC, tokens minted for max 10 minutes; rotation done via orchestration job every 6 hours for long-lived agents.
5) sdlc_runbook_v3.pdf — internal runbook with a redaction layer for troubleshooting logs; table of contents and gating criteria visible.

I will attach CSV + policy snapshot + run samples + memo + runbook to the outbound to Amanda. Two questions:
- Rishi, do we need to include HSM/KMS audit logs or is the Vault OIDC proof enough for FedFin?
- Hannah, should the CSV include drafts flagged in "awaiting-approval" state or only approved/completed changes? Current ask suggests last 12 months of changes including pending; I can filter to approved+completed only if preferred.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. InfoSec Analyst — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SIG / FedFin: Request for SDLC artifacts (change-control + CI guardrails)

Amanda — attaching requested artifacts. Summary below for reviewers and a short note on redactions.

Attachments (attached to this email):
- sdlc_runbook_v3.pdf (internal runbook; troubleshooting logs redacted)
- ci_pipeline_policy_snapshot_20281020.txt (policy rules + enforcement configuration)
- change-approvals-audit-trail.csv (last 12 months; includes approved and completed changes only)

Evidence highlights:
- PR gating is enforced via our policy engine; pipeline-run samples included (rdw-20281005-1182 shows secret-scan terminated pipeline on detection; rdw-20281018-1307 shows a successful enforce-and-approve flow).
- Ephemeral credential process: CI agents use OIDC to request short-lived Vault tokens (max TTL 10m); memo included (ephemeral-creds-memo.txt).
- Change log: CSV rows include approver identity and timestamps. Redactions: branch_compare_uri and internal_notes removed for confidentiality.

If you'd like signed attestations for any of the pipeline runs or a KMS audit extract, we can provide those on request — flag which runs you want signed.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Trust & Risk — Redwood Inference
